A more organized band of showers is pushing into\nportions of the northern and central panhandle Tuesday morning.\nAnother organized band is likely to push through late Tuesday\nnight through Wednesday. The Winter Weather Advisories have been\nexpanded further southward given expected heavier precipitation\nrates leading to a transition to more snow. Advisories could be\nupgraded to Winter Storm Warnings if heavier snow showers continue\nover the same area.\n\n* WHAT...For the first Winter Weather Advisory, snow. Additional\nsnow accumulations of up to two inches. For the second Winter\nWeather Advisory, snow expected. Total snow accumulations for\nthe second advisory of 3 to 6 inches.\n\n* WHERE...Haines Borough and Klukwan.\n\n* WHEN...For the first Winter Weather Advisory, until 10 AM AKDT\nthis morning. For the second Winter Weather Advisory, from 4\nAM to 7 PM AKDT Wednesday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult and is discouraged.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A band of snow showers moves through on\nTuesday. Another band will move through late Tuesday night\ninto Wednesday The convective nature of snow showers will\nresult in variable accumulations.",

                "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.\n\nDo not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles.                 "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued March 17 at 8:54AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
                "description": "An unseasonably strong area of high pressure aloft is expected to\nmove across the Desert Southwest through at least the weekend.\nTemperatures will climb each afternoon, with the lowlands reaching\nwell into the 90s by Thursday. Saturday is expected to be the\nhottest day of the week, followed by a minor cool down. Afternoon\nhigh temperatures will be 20 to 25 degrees above seasonal averages,\nand will be more reminiscent of late May or early June. All-time\ntemperature records for the month of March will be broken.\n\nThe abnormality of these high temperatures will increase health\nrisks, especially for populations more susceptible to heat-related\nhealth issues.\n\nPeople are encouraged to reduce outdoor activity during the\nafternoon hours, wear light-colored loose-fitting clothing, drink\nplenty of water, and wear sunscreen.",

                "senderName": "NWS San Juan PR",
                "headline": "Rip Current Statement issued March 17 at 10:05AM AST until March 18 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR",
                "description": "* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.\n\n* WHERE...Along the exposed beaches in northern, eastern and\nsouthern Puerto Rico, Culebra, Vieques, and the US Virgin\nIslands.\n\n* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away\nfrom shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to\nreturn to safety.",
                "instruction": "There is a high risk of rip currents.\n\nRip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away\nfrom shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the\nsandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties\nand piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and\nsigns.\n\nIf you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain\ncalm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for\nhelp. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to\nshore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to\nswim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.",
                "response": "Avoid",

                "description": "* WHAT...High temperatures in the low to mid 90s across the interior\nand 80s along the coastline.\n\n* WHERE...The Bay Area and Central Coast.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to\nheat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate\nhydration. Portions of the interior Central Coast may reach the\nupper 90s starting mid to late week. The risk of heat related illnesses will increase with\neach additional day of heating from this event.",
                "instruction": "Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and\nif possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.\n\nTake extra precautions when outside.
